It supports scripting and interactive commands like `clean`, `create partition primary`, `format fs=ntfs quick`, and `assign letter=X`. `chkdsk` checks volume health, `defrag` optimizes clusters, and `sfc` checks system files.

distractor_analysis.1: `chkdsk` scans file systems and disk sectors for corruption and bad blocks.
distractor_analysis.2: `defrag` reorganizes fragmented file pieces on magnetic hard drives.
distractor_analysis.3: `sfc` inspects protected Windows operating system DLLs and binaries.

video_reference.title: Windows Command Line Tools - CompTIA A+ 220-1202 - 1.5

core2.question: A technician is enabling Hyper-V on a Windows 11 Pro workstation to host test virtual machines. Which hardware CPU feature must be supported by the processor and enabled in UEFI?
options: An integrated GPU for the console session
An XMP memory profile enabled in UEFI
Hardware virtualization, Intel VT-x or AMD-V, together with SLAT
Hyper-Threading enabled in UEFI setup
core2.explanation: Client Hyper-V requires a 64-bit processor with Second Level Address Translation (SLAT) and hardware virtualization extensions (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) enabled in the system UEFI/BIOS. Hyper-Threading, integrated graphics, and XMP memory overclocking are not mandatory virtualization prerequisites.

distractor_analysis.1: Hyper-Threading adds logical cores. It is not required for the hypervisor to run.
distractor_analysis.2: Hyper-V renders guest video in software. No integrated GPU is required.
distractor_analysis.3: XMP sets memory timings. It has no bearing on virtualization support.

video_reference.title: An Overview of Windows - CompTIA A+ 220-1202 - 1.3

core2.question: Which Linux command-line tool transfers data to or from a network server using protocols like HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP, making it ideal for API testing and file downloads?
options: `kill`
`curl`
`ls`
`chmod`
core2.explanation: `curl` (Client URL) is a versatile command-line utility used to send and receive data over network protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SFTP), widely used for testing REST APIs, downloading files, and inspecting HTTP headers. `ls` lists files, `chmod` changes permissions, and `kill` terminates processes.

distractor_analysis.1: `ls` lists directory contents in the file system.
distractor_analysis.2: `chmod` modifies file read, write, and execute permissions.
distractor_analysis.3: `kill` sends process signals to terminate running application PIDs.

core2.question: A visitor follows closely behind an employee through a badge-controlled datacenter security door without scanning an authorized credential. What physical security breach is this?
options: Shoulder surfing
Tailgating / Piggybacking
Quishing
Dumpster diving
core2.explanation: Tailgating (or piggybacking) is a physical social engineering breach where an unauthorized individual slips through an electronic badge-controlled door by closely following an authorized employee. Shoulder surfing is looking at screens, quishing uses QR codes, and dumpster diving searches trash.

distractor_analysis.0: Shoulder surfing involves visually spying on passwords or screens in close proximity.
distractor_analysis.2: Quishing delivers malicious phishing links via QR code images.
distractor_analysis.3: Dumpster diving searches waste containers for sensitive documents.

core2.question: Which access control method BEST implements the principle of least privilege for a junior operator who only needs to reset domain user passwords?
options: Add the operator to the Domain Admins group
Delegate password-reset rights on the target OU using role-based access control
Grant the operator Account Operators group membership
Grant Full Control on all Active Directory partitions
core2.explanation: Delegating specific administrative permissions (such as password resets) within a designated Organizational Unit (OU) using Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) grants the junior operator only the exact privileges required for their job duties, strictly enforcing least privilege. Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, and root Full Control grant excessive domain-wide authority.

distractor_analysis.0: Domain Admins grants control of the whole forest for a task that needs one permission.
distractor_analysis.2: Account Operators is close but still allows creating and deleting accounts across the domain.
distractor_analysis.3: Full Control on every partition is the widest grant available and fails least privilege outright.

core2.question: Corporate Wi-Fi for staff laptops should use which modern wireless encryption and authentication standard combining AES encryption and 802.1X RADIUS authentication?
options: WEP-Open
WPA3-Enterprise or WPA2-Enterprise
WPA-Personal (TKIP)
WPS with static PIN
core2.explanation: WPA2-Enterprise and WPA3-Enterprise utilize IEEE 802.1X port-based authentication connected to a backend RADIUS server with AES encryption, ensuring that every user authenticates with unique individual credentials or certificates. WEP is broken, WPA-Personal uses a shared passphrase, and WPS is vulnerable to PIN brute-forcing.

distractor_analysis.0: WEP is an obsolete, insecure protocol broken by static RC4 key reuse.
distractor_analysis.2: WPA-Personal relies on a shared passphrase and uses deprecated TKIP encryption.
distractor_analysis.3: WPS is an insecure automated pairing feature vulnerable to brute-force PIN attacks.

core2.question: Malware that encrypts files on local and network drives and demands cryptocurrency payment in exchange for a private decryption key is classified as what?
options: Adware, unwanted advertising injected into the browser
Ransomware, files encrypted pending a crypto payment
Spyware, silent collection of user activity
Keylogger, capture of every keystroke typed
core2.explanation: Ransomware (specifically crypto-malware) locks or encrypts user files using strong cryptographic algorithms and demands an extortion payment (usually Bitcoin or other cryptocurrency) to obtain the decryption key. Adware displays ads, spyware tracks browsing, and keyloggers record keystrokes.

distractor_analysis.0: Adware is a nuisance that monetises impressions. It does not encrypt data or demand payment.
distractor_analysis.2: Spyware exfiltrates information quietly and wants to stay unnoticed, so it does not announce itself.
distractor_analysis.3: A keylogger captures typing to steal credentials. It leaves files readable.

core2.question: A CFO receives an email appearing to come from the CEO directing an urgent, confidential wire transfer to a foreign supplier account to close an acquisition. What social engineering attack is this?
options: Shoulder surfing in the executive suite
Dumpster diving for discarded documents
A watering hole attack on a supplier site
Business email compromise, also called whaling
core2.explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) and Whaling are targeted social engineering attacks that impersonate senior executives or business partners to manipulate financial personnel into authorizing fraudulent wire transfers or disclosing confidential data. Shoulder surfing is visual spying, dumpster diving is rummaging through trash, and watering hole attacks compromise websites.

distractor_analysis.1: Shoulder surfing requires physical line of sight to a screen or keypad.
distractor_analysis.2: Dumpster diving recovers discarded paper or media, not an inbound email.
distractor_analysis.3: A watering hole compromises a site the target visits, rather than impersonating an executive.

core2.question: Which Windows security feature encrypts entire storage volumes (including the operating system and system files) to protect data at rest against offline physical theft?
options: Windows Defender SmartScreen
Disk Defragmenter
BitLocker Drive Encryption
User Account Control (UAC)
core2.explanation: BitLocker Drive Encryption provides full volume encryption (FVE) on Windows Pro and Enterprise editions. It encrypts the entire volume using AES and integrates with the motherboard TPM chip to protect data against offline attacks if the drive is physically removed. UAC manages elevation prompts, SmartScreen blocks malicious URLs, and Defragmenter optimizes disks.

distractor_analysis.1: UAC enforces privilege boundaries during an active Windows session but does not encrypt storage blocks.
distractor_analysis.2: SmartScreen warns users about untrusted download files and phishing websites.
distractor_analysis.3: Disk Defragmenter reorganizes file clusters on spinning magnetic disks.

core2.question: After verifying that a workstation is infected with active malware, what is the FIRST action the technician must take according to the CompTIA malware removal methodology?
options: Disable the local firewall so the scanner can update
Enable System Restore and take a fresh checkpoint
Educate the end user on safe browsing habits
Quarantine the host from wired and wireless networks
core2.explanation: Step 2 of the CompTIA 7-step malware removal process is to Quarantine the infected system by disconnecting Ethernet cables and disabling Wi-Fi/Bluetooth, isolating the host to prevent lateral malware movement. Educating users is Step 7, firewalls should not be disabled, and enabling System Restore is Step 6.

distractor_analysis.0: User education is the final step in the methodology, once the machine is clean.
distractor_analysis.2: Dropping the firewall widens the attack surface while the host is still infected.
distractor_analysis.3: System Restore is disabled during remediation so malware cannot survive in a restore point.

core2.question: Which authentication approach requires presenting credentials from at least two different factor categories (e.g., 'Something you know' combined with 'Something you have')?
options: Single-factor authentication
Multifactor authentication (MFA)
Anonymous authentication
Password complexity policy
core2.explanation: Multifactor Authentication (MFA) requires presenting two or more independent credentials from different authentication categories: Something you know (password/PIN), Something you have (smart card/hardware token), or Something you are (biometrics). Single-factor uses one category, anonymous uses no credentials, and password complexity is a password policy.

distractor_analysis.0: Single-factor authentication relies on credentials from only one category (e.g., password only).
distractor_analysis.2: Anonymous authentication permits unauthenticated access without verifying identity.
distractor_analysis.3: Password complexity policies govern password length and characters within a single knowledge factor.

core2.question: Degaussing or industrial physical shredding of decommissioned hard disk drives is an example of which security procedure?
options: Logical data recovery
Physical data destruction / media sanitization
In-place OS upgrade
Volume defragmentation
core2.explanation: Degaussing and physical shredding are physical data destruction and media sanitization methods designed to permanently destroy data stored on magnetic or solid-state media so it can never be recovered. Data recovery retrieves lost files, OS upgrades update software, and defragmentation reorganizes clusters.

distractor_analysis.0: Data recovery is the process of restoring lost files from damaged drives, the opposite of intentional destruction.
distractor_analysis.2: In-place OS upgrades update the operating system while preserving existing user files.
distractor_analysis.3: Volume defragmentation reorganizes file fragments on spinning disks to optimize read speeds.

core2.question: A user encounters a red browser warning stating 'Your connection is not private' when visiting an internal company portal. What is the MOST common root cause?
options: The computer display monitor is unplugged
The mouse DPI setting is too high
The workstation power supply is failing
Expired, untrusted, or mismatched SSL/TLS digital certificate
core2.explanation: Browser TLS/HTTPS security warnings occur when the website's SSL/TLS digital certificate has expired, was issued by an untrusted Certificate Authority (CA) whose root certificate is missing from the client trust store, or does not match the domain name in the URL (Common Name mismatch). Hardware monitors, mice, and power supplies do not cause TLS cryptographic warnings.

distractor_analysis.1: An unplugged display monitor results in a black screen, not a browser software certificate error.
distractor_analysis.2: Mouse DPI settings adjust pointer tracking sensitivity on the desktop.
distractor_analysis.3: Power supply hardware faults cause sudden system shutdowns, not web browser cryptographic errors.

core2.question: Which Active Directory component applies password policies, account lockouts, software restrictions, and desktop settings centrally across thousands of domain workstations?
options: Local HOSTS file
Static DNS MX record
DHCP Reservation
Group Policy Object (GPO)
core2.explanation: Group Policy Objects (GPOs) in Active Directory allow administrators to centrally manage, configure, and enforce security policies, password complexity rules, software restrictions, and system settings across domain-joined computers and users. HOSTS files map local IPs, MX records route email, and DHCP reservations assign static IP addresses.

distractor_analysis.1: The local HOSTS file maps static IP addresses to hostnames on a single individual computer.
distractor_analysis.2: A DNS MX record specifies the mail exchange servers responsible for accepting incoming email.
distractor_analysis.3: A DHCP reservation assigns a fixed IP address to a specific network MAC address.

core2.question: Evil Twin rogue wireless access points primarily enable which class of cyberattack by tricking victims into connecting?
options: Physical hard drive degaussing
RAM chip soldering degradation
On-path / wireless eavesdropping and credential harvesting
Hardware CPU destruction
core2.explanation: An Evil Twin access point mimics a legitimate Wi-Fi network's SSID to trick clients into connecting. Once connected, all client traffic routes through the attacker's rogue AP, enabling on-path (Man-in-the-Middle) eavesdropping, packet sniffing, SSL stripping, and credential harvesting. It cannot physically alter CPU silicon, degauss drives, or damage RAM soldering.

distractor_analysis.1: Wireless network connections cannot cause physical silicon destruction of the client computer processor.
distractor_analysis.2: Degaussing requires powerful physical electromagnetic fields applied directly to magnetic storage platters.
distractor_analysis.3: Connecting to a rogue Wi-Fi access point has no physical impact on motherboard RAM solder joints.

core2.question: Which mobile security control allows an IT administrator to securely erase all data from a lost or stolen corporate smartphone over the cellular network?
options: NFC pairing
Remote wipe via MDM
Local biometric lock
Bluetooth tethering
core2.explanation: Mobile Device Management (MDM) platforms provide remote wipe functionality, allowing administrators to send a cryptographic erase command over cellular or Wi-Fi networks to sanitize all data on a lost or stolen device. Biometric locks require physical presence, tethering shares internet, and NFC is short-range tap communication.

distractor_analysis.1: Biometric locks (fingerprint/face) authenticate physical users at the lock screen but cannot initiate network wipe commands.
distractor_analysis.2: Bluetooth tethering shares a cellular internet connection with nearby paired devices.
distractor_analysis.3: NFC pairing establishes short-range (under 4 cm) communication for mobile payments and device pairing.

core2.question: When deploying a brand-new SOHO router and firewall, what should the administrator do with the factory default administrator password?
options: Leave it set to the factory default for easier remote tech support
Change it immediately to a strong, unique administrative password and store it securely
Disable all passwords on the router
Write the password on a public whiteboard
core2.explanation: Leaving factory default credentials (e.g., admin/admin, admin/password) on a router is a severe security vulnerability that automated bots and attackers exploit within minutes. The administrator must immediately change default credentials to a strong, unique passphrase. Leaving defaults, disabling passwords, or posting them publicly invites compromise.

distractor_analysis.0: Leaving default credentials allows automated internet worms and attackers to easily seize control of the router.
distractor_analysis.2: Disabling administrative passwords removes all authentication protection from the management console.
distractor_analysis.3: Displaying administrative credentials on a public whiteboard violates physical and operational security standards.

video_reference.title: Securing a SOHO Network - CompTIA A+ 220-1202 - 2.10

core2.question: A vendor advisory lands in the ticket queue warning that attacks are already being seen in the wild and no fix is available yet. A zero-day vulnerability is characterized by which condition?
options: The vulnerability was patched ten years ago
The vulnerability only affects legacy dial-up modems
The vulnerability occurs only on the first day of every month
The vulnerability is actively exploited before the software vendor has developed and released an official security patch
core2.explanation: A zero-day vulnerability refers to a software security flaw that is known to attackers or actively exploited in the wild before the software developer has created and distributed an official security patch (leaving zero days of protection). It does not refer to calendar dates, patched legacy bugs, or dial-up modems.

distractor_analysis.1: Patched vulnerabilities are known, historical flaws for which remediation updates already exist.
distractor_analysis.2: Zero-day vulnerabilities can affect any software, operating system, or firmware application.
distractor_analysis.3: The term 'zero-day' reflects the absence of patch lead time, not calendar days of the month.

core2.question: In Windows NTFS permissions, what specific capability does Full Control grant that Modify permission does NOT grant?
options: Changing file permissions and taking file ownership
Deleting files and folders
Executing executable programs
Reading file contents
core2.explanation: In NTFS permissions, the Modify permission allows reading, writing, executing, and deleting files and subfolders. However, only Full Control grants the special rights to Change Permissions (modify ACLs) and Take Ownership of the file or folder. Read, delete, and execute are included in Modify.

distractor_analysis.0: Reading file contents is granted by standard Read permissions as well as Modify.
distractor_analysis.2: Deleting files and subdirectories is explicitly included in the NTFS Modify permission.
distractor_analysis.3: Executing application binaries is included in the Read & Execute and Modify permissions.

core2.question: Which protocol is standard for providing centralized Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) for 802.1X wireless networks and VPNs over UDP?
options: FTP
Telnet
SMTP
RADIUS
core2.explanation: RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) provides centralized AAA management for network access clients, VPNs, and 802.1X wireless networks over UDP. FTP transfers files, Telnet is unencrypted CLI, and SMTP transfers email.

distractor_analysis.1: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) transfers files over TCP ports 20/21 and does not provide network AAA services.
distractor_analysis.2: Telnet operates on TCP port 23 for unencrypted command-line sessions.
distractor_analysis.3: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) routes electronic mail messages between mail servers.

core2.question: A hardware or software keylogger installed on an employee workstation is designed primarily to steal what type of information?
options: Motherboard fan speeds
Keystrokes, passwords, and sensitive typed text
Physical CPU clock speeds
Monitor display refresh rates
core2.explanation: Keyloggers (software spyware or hardware inline USB devices) covertly record every keystroke pressed on the physical keyboard, capturing user account credentials, credit card numbers, confidential messages, and search queries. They do not monitor CPU clock frequencies, refresh rates, or fan speeds.

distractor_analysis.1: CPU clock speeds are hardware telemetry metrics managed by motherboard firmware, not targets of keyloggers.
distractor_analysis.2: Monitor refresh rates are video display settings, not sensitive typed user input.
distractor_analysis.3: Fan speeds are managed by thermal hardware controllers, having zero relationship with typed keystrokes.

core2.question: A supply chain attack compromises an organization's security by targeting which vector?
options: The building's janitorial cleaning supplies
Local coffee shop menu boards
Workstation mouse pads
Trusted third-party vendors, software update pipelines, or hardware suppliers
core2.explanation: A supply chain attack compromises a target organization indirectly by infiltrating trusted third-party suppliers, upstream software development repositories, code-signing certificates, or hardware vendors (e.g., injecting malicious backdoors into legitimate vendor software updates). Janitorial supplies, menus, and mouse pads are not IT supply chain attack vectors.

distractor_analysis.1: Janitorial cleaning supplies are physical facility maintenance items and do not compromise IT software supply chains.
distractor_analysis.2: Coffee shop menu boards are external public displays unrelated to enterprise software delivery pipelines.
distractor_analysis.3: Mouse pads are passive physical desk accessories without computational logic.

core2.question: Which security practice BEST hardens a web browser used by datacenter engineers to manage cloud infrastructure administrative consoles?
options: Keep the browser updated to the latest patched version, limit extensions to verified tools, and enforce MFA
Disable all browser certificate validation warnings
Save all administrative passwords in plaintext on the desktop
Install dozens of unverified third-party shopping extensions
core2.explanation: Securing web browsers used for administrative consoles requires applying regular browser updates and patches, disabling or removing unnecessary third-party extensions, using dedicated administrative browser profiles, enforcing MFA, and respecting HTTPS certificate warnings. Unverified extensions, ignoring certificate alerts, and plaintext passwords create massive vulnerabilities.

distractor_analysis.0: Installing unverified browser add-ons dramatically increases the attack surface and risks credential theft via malicious extensions.
distractor_analysis.2: Disabling certificate validation warnings exposes administrative sessions to on-path (MitM) eavesdropping.
distractor_analysis.3: Storing administrative passwords in plaintext files on the desktop violates basic credential management security.

core2.question: What is the MOST effective physical countermeasure against shoulder surfing when an employee is working on sensitive documents in an airport lounge?
options: Disabling the laptop Wi-Fi card
Increasing the display brightness to maximum
Changing the desktop wallpaper to bright yellow
Installing an anti-glare physical privacy filter screen over the laptop display
core2.explanation: Physical privacy filters (privacy screens) fit over laptop displays and use micro-louver technology to restrict the viewing angle, making the screen appear completely black from side angles and preventing nearby people from viewing sensitive text (shoulder surfing). Disabling Wi-Fi, increasing brightness, and changing wallpapers do not restrict side viewing angles.

distractor_analysis.1: Disabling Wi-Fi disconnects network access but leaves open local documents completely visible to anyone standing nearby.
distractor_analysis.2: Increasing screen brightness makes text easier for nearby bystanders to read from a distance.
distractor_analysis.3: Changing desktop wallpaper colors does not obscure active application windows containing confidential data.

core2.question: Which native Windows security component provides real-time signature-based and behavioral anti-malware scanning for all installed applications and downloaded files?
options: Character Map
Microsoft Defender Antivirus
Windows Media Player
Disk Defragmenter
core2.explanation: Microsoft Defender Antivirus is the built-in anti-malware solution integrated into Windows 10 and 11, providing continuous real-time scanning, cloud-delivered behavioral protection, and signature updates. Media Player plays video/audio, Defragmenter optimizes hard drives, and Character Map displays font symbols.

distractor_analysis.1: Windows Media Player is an entertainment application for multimedia playback.
distractor_analysis.2: Disk Defragmenter optimizes file cluster placement on magnetic hard drives.
distractor_analysis.3: Character Map is a utility used to locate and copy special typographic font characters.

core2.question: Why is a Rootkit considered one of the most dangerous forms of malware on a corporate workstation?
options: It encrypts user documents and demands payment for the decryption key
It floods the local segment with broadcast traffic until the network stalls
It replaces the browser home page and injects advertising
It runs with kernel privileges and hides its processes and files from security tools
core2.explanation: Rootkits are exceptionally dangerous because they execute at Ring 0 (kernel space) or bootloader level, subverting the operating system itself to intercept API calls and hide their files, network connections, and processes from antivirus scanners and Task Manager. They do not merely delete wallpapers, display benign ads, or improve performance.

distractor_analysis.1: That is ransomware. It is destructive but visible, which makes it easier to detect than a rootkit.
distractor_analysis.2: Broadcast flooding is a denial of service symptom, not a stealth persistence technique.
distractor_analysis.3: Browser hijacking is adware behaviour and is removed with standard cleanup tools.

core2.question: Why is obtaining a formal Certificate of Destruction essential when an organization contracts a third-party vendor to shred decommissioned hard disk drives?
options: It provides a 100% discount on future hardware purchases
It allows the company to reuse the shredded drive platters
It provides legally recognized proof of proper media sanitization for regulatory compliance audits (e.g., HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GDPR)
It automatically updates the Windows registry on all client PCs
core2.explanation: A Certificate of Destruction provides legally binding documentation detailing the serial numbers, destruction method (shredding/incineration), date/time, and authorized witness signatures for destroyed media. This document is required to prove compliance during regulatory audits (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GDPR, SOX). It does not update registries, grant discounts, or allow reusing shredded scrap metal.

distractor_analysis.1: A physical paper certificate of destruction has no interaction with operating system registry hives.
distractor_analysis.2: Certificates of destruction are compliance records, not commercial discount coupons for hardware vendors.
distractor_analysis.3: Shredded hard drive platters are destroyed into tiny metal fragments and cannot be reconstructed or reused.

core2.question: How does an attacker successfully execute a SQL Injection (SQLi) attack against a web application database?
options: By sending standard ICMP ping packets to port 80
By inputting unfiltered SQL query statements into vulnerable web form input fields to manipulate backend database commands
By cutting the physical fiber optic cable connecting to the web server
By setting the browser zoom level to 200%
core2.explanation: SQL Injection (SQLi) occurs when a web application fails to properly sanitize or parameterize user input, allowing an attacker to inject malicious SQL commands (e.g., `' OR '1'='1`) into input fields or URL parameters to bypass authentication, dump database contents, or modify records. Cutting cables is physical sabotage, zoom levels change display size, and ICMP pings test network reachability.

distractor_analysis.1: Cutting physical network cabling causes a denial of service at the physical layer, not a software SQL injection vulnerability.
distractor_analysis.2: Adjusting browser zoom modifies visual magnification on the client display without altering web server query syntax.
distractor_analysis.3: ICMP ping packets operate at layer 3 and do not interact with application layer database query parameters.

core2.question: What is the primary objective of a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack against a web application?
options: To inject SQL into a form field so the database returns extra rows
To flood the server with half-open TCP connections until it stops responding
To make the browser submit an authenticated request the user did not intend
To inject client-side script into a trusted site so it runs in other users' browsers
core2.explanation: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks exploit improper input sanitization in web applications to inject malicious client-side JavaScript into web pages viewed by other users. When victims view the page, their browser executes the script, allowing the attacker to steal session cookies, hijack account tokens, or redirect users to phishing sites. XSS does not overheat CPUs, alter magnetic storage, or flash router firmware.

distractor_analysis.1: That is SQL injection. It targets the database tier, not the visitor's browser.
distractor_analysis.2: That is a SYN flood, a denial of service technique with no script execution.
distractor_analysis.3: That is cross-site request forgery. It abuses an existing session rather than running attacker script.

core2.question: For SOHO router hardening, applying regular firmware updates primarily addresses which operational requirement?
options: Extending the DHCP scope so more clients can lease an address
Adding new QoS queues for voice traffic on the WAN interface
Patching known vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows and remote execution bugs
Raising the wireless throughput available to older client radios
core2.explanation: Router firmware updates patch discovered software vulnerabilities, fix routing bugs, close known remote code execution holes, and update wireless security protocols (e.g., adding WPA3). Firmware has no interaction with monitor colors, keyboard polling, or audio bitrates.

distractor_analysis.1: Throughput is set by the radio standard the client supports, not by patch level.
distractor_analysis.2: Scope size is a configuration change you make yourself; it is not what a firmware update delivers.
distractor_analysis.3: QoS may appear as a feature, but hardening is about closing known vulnerabilities.

video_reference.title: Securing a SOHO Network - CompTIA A+ 220-1202 - 2.10

core2.question: How does implementing Just-In-Time (JIT) privileged access management reduce operational cybersecurity risk?
options: By exempting administrative portals from multifactor authentication
By granting elevated rights only when approved, and revoking them straight afterwards
By making every administrator a permanent member of Domain Admins
By sharing one root password among the technicians on shift
core2.explanation: Just-In-Time (JIT) access reduces the attack surface by eliminating standing administrative privileges. Users operate with standard privileges until an elevated task is required, at which point elevated rights are granted for a restricted duration (e.g., 2 hours) with full auditing and automatic revocation upon task completion. Permanent domain rights and shared root passwords create massive vulnerabilities.

distractor_analysis.1: Standing membership is exactly the always-on privilege that JIT exists to remove.
distractor_analysis.2: A shared credential destroys attribution, so nobody can say who made a change.
distractor_analysis.3: Removing MFA weakens the most valuable accounts on the estate.

core2.question: A security lead is briefing the help desk on threat categories after a data leak traced back to an internal account. Which characteristic defines an insider threat?
options: External nation-state groups that rely on zero-day exploits for entry
Automated botnets brute forcing exposed remote desktop services
Supply chain compromise of a vendor update pushed to customers
Current or former staff, contractors or partners who misuse legitimate access
core2.explanation: An Insider Threat originates from an individual who has authorized, legitimate access to an organization's network, facilities, or data (such as employees, contractors, or vendors) and misuses that access maliciously or inadvertently to cause harm, exfiltrate IP, or disrupt operations. Nation-states are external threats, and power/rodent events are physical/environmental hazards.

distractor_analysis.1: Nation-state actors are an external advanced threat. The defining trait of an insider is authorized access.
distractor_analysis.2: Botnet brute force is external and unauthenticated by definition.
distractor_analysis.3: Supply chain compromise abuses vendor trust, not the access rights of a person inside the organization.

core2.question: What security risk is directly mitigated by configuring an automatic screen lock policy after five minutes of inactivity across corporate workstations?
options: Brute force attempts against the domain account lockout policy
Malware persistence through a scheduled task that runs at logon
Unauthorized access to an unattended session that is still logged in
Credential replay from a Kerberos ticket captured on the wire
core2.explanation: Enforcing automatic screen locking after a brief period of inactivity ensures that if a user walks away from their desk, the workstation locks itself and requires re-authentication, preventing unauthorized personnel from accessing open confidential data or impersonating the user. It has no effect on RAID rebuilds, Wi-Fi interference, or UPS power.

distractor_analysis.1: Ticket replay is countered by Kerberos timestamps and encryption, not by a screen timeout.
distractor_analysis.2: Lockout thresholds and password policy handle brute force. A locked screen does not change that.
distractor_analysis.3: Persistence is removed by remediation and autorun review, not by locking the console.

core2.question: How does a 'Password Spraying' attack differ from a traditional brute-force password attack?
options: Password spraying only attacks WEP initialization vectors
Password spraying attempts a few common passwords across many user accounts to avoid triggering account lockout thresholds
Password spraying attempts millions of passwords against a single user account as quickly as possible
Password spraying exclusively uses rainbow tables offline
core2.explanation: Password spraying is a horizontal attack where the adversary tests a small number of commonly used passwords (e.g., 'Winter2026!') across hundreds or thousands of different user accounts. This avoids exceeding individual account lockout thresholds (e.g., locking after 5 failed attempts on a single account). Traditional brute-force attacks test many passwords against a single targeted account.

distractor_analysis.1: Testing millions of passwords against a single account is a classic vertical brute-force attack, which quickly triggers account lockouts.
distractor_analysis.2: Rainbow tables are precomputed hash lookup tables used for offline password cracking, not online spraying.
distractor_analysis.3: Attacking WEP IVs is an obsolete wireless packet-injection attack.

core2.question: Disabling the built-in Guest account, disabling unused local accounts, and renaming the default Administrator account are examples of which cybersecurity process?
options: Hardware overclocking
Network cable certification
Monitor color calibration
Operating system security hardening best practices
core2.explanation: System hardening involves configuring operating system and service settings to minimize the attack surface by eliminating default vulnerabilities, such as disabling unnecessary guest accounts, renaming known default administrative accounts, closing unused ports, and applying strict security policies. Overclocking boosts clock speeds, cable certification tests wiring, and calibration adjusts display colors.

distractor_analysis.1: Hardware overclocking increases CPU/GPU clock frequencies beyond factory ratings to boost raw compute throughput.
distractor_analysis.2: Network cable certification uses specialized TDR/fluke testers to verify Cat6/6A wire map and attenuation standards.
distractor_analysis.3: Color calibration aligns display RGB profiles for professional graphic print accuracy.

core2.question: When does Full Device Encryption (FDE) on corporate smartphones and tablets protect stored corporate data from extraction?
options: When developer USB debugging is enabled and connected to untrusted computers
When third-party app sideloading is permitted without restriction
When the device is powered off or locked with a strong passcode/biometric authentication
When the device is left unlocked on a public table
core2.explanation: Full Device Encryption (FDE) protects data at rest by securing cryptographic keys inside hardware security modules (Secure Enclave / Titan chip). When the device is powered off or locked, the keys are locked in memory, rendering flash storage unreadable without the user's passcode or biometric validation. Leaving screens unlocked, enabling unauthenticated USB debugging, and unvetted sideloading compromise this protection.

distractor_analysis.1: If the screen is left unlocked, the cryptographic keys reside in active RAM and data is freely readable by anyone holding the device.
distractor_analysis.2: Unrestricted USB debugging permits extraction of application data via command-line ADB bridge tools.
distractor_analysis.3: Sideloading unverified applications introduces malware that can execute within user space while the device is unlocked.

core2.question: A Windows workstation frequently crashes with a Blue Screen stop code `MEMORY_MANAGEMENT`. Which physical hardware subsystem should the technician test FIRST?
options: Mouse optical sensor DPI
System RAM modules using Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86
USB headset audio equalization profiles
Display monitor color profile
core2.explanation: The `MEMORY_MANAGEMENT` stop error (bugcheck `0x0000001A`) indicates that the Windows memory manager detected a severe memory corruption or parity fault, almost always caused by defective, overheating, or mismatched physical RAM modules. Running memory diagnostics (e.g., `mdsched.exe`) and testing individual DIMMs isolates bad RAM. Headsets, monitors, and mice do not cause kernel memory management stop codes.

distractor_analysis.1: Headset EQ presets operate at user-level audio software layers and cannot cause kernel memory manager stop errors.
distractor_analysis.2: Monitor color profiles manage RGB lookup tables in display software and do not cause physical memory errors.
distractor_analysis.3: Mouse DPI settings govern optical tracking speed and have zero relation to RAM silicon hardware integrity.

core2.question: Following a recent software update, a corporate CRM application crashes immediately upon launch. What is the MOST appropriate initial software troubleshooting procedure?
options: Reimage every workstation in the entire company
Inspect the Event Viewer Application log for crash details and repair the application or roll back the update
Replace the core datacenter Top-of-Rack network switch
Add two additional batteries to the facility UPS
core2.explanation: When an application crashes post-update, checking Event Viewer (Application log for Event ID 1000) reveals the faulting module, exception code, and DLL. Technicians can then perform an in-place software repair via Settings/Control Panel or uninstall/roll back the problematic update. Reimaging all PCs, replacing network switches, and adding UPS batteries are completely unnecessary and disruptive.

distractor_analysis.0: Reimaging the entire enterprise company fleet is an extreme, unwarranted overreaction for a single software update glitch.
distractor_analysis.2: Top-of-Rack switches handle datacenter Ethernet packet switching and have no connection to local client application crashes.
distractor_analysis.3: UPS batteries provide emergency backup power during AC outages and do not resolve software update bugs.

core2.question: A corporate mobile application freezes and force-closes repeatedly on an Android tablet. What is the recommended first-level user troubleshooting step?
options: Replace the datacenter power distribution unit (PDU)
Reflash network switch ASICs
Degauss the tablet with an industrial electromagnet
Force stop the application and clear the app cache/data in Settings -> Apps
core2.explanation: When an isolated mobile app misbehaves or crashes, the first step is force-closing the application and clearing its cached temporary files in Settings -> Apps. If that fails, uninstalling and reinstalling the app resolves corrupted data. PDU replacement, switch flashing, and degaussing are absurd and destructive.

distractor_analysis.1: Datacenter PDUs distribute AC power to server racks and have zero connection to local mobile app memory crashes.
distractor_analysis.2: Reflashing switch ASICs is a network infrastructure maintenance task unrelated to mobile application software.
distractor_analysis.3: Applying a degausser to a mobile tablet will permanently destroy the display, inductive coils, and internal electronics.

core2.question: Windows Update fails repeatedly on a client workstation with error code `0x80070002`. Which built-in recovery steps should the technician execute first?
options: Physically remove half the RAM from the motherboard
Set the motherboard BIOS date back thirty years
Run the Windows Update Troubleshooter and reset the SoftwareDistribution cache folder
Disable the network adapter permanently
core2.explanation: Windows Update errors often stem from corrupted cached download files in `%WinDir%\SoftwareDistribution` or stopped background services (BITS, wuauserv, cryptsvc). Running the Windows Update Troubleshooter (Settings -> Troubleshoot) and resetting update components clears stuck states. Disabling NICs, pulling RAM, and falsifying system dates break system functionality.

distractor_analysis.1: Disabling the network adapter cuts off all internet connectivity, preventing Windows Update from downloading any updates.
distractor_analysis.2: Removing functional RAM reduces system memory without addressing corrupted Windows Update temporary download files.
distractor_analysis.3: Falsifying the system date breaks TLS/SSL certificate validation and prevents all secure HTTPS updates.

core2.question: A user reports extreme system sluggishness, with Task Manager showing 100% active disk utilization on a mechanical HDD. What is the BEST immediate software mitigation while planning a hardware SSD upgrade?
options: Disconnect power while the system is writing data
Inspect Task Manager for high-I/O processes, disable unnecessary startup applications, and scan for malware
Unplug the CPU cooling fan
Disable virtual memory paging entirely without performance analysis
core2.explanation: 100% disk utilization on spinning HDDs is commonly caused by startup application bloat, background Windows Search indexing storms, SysMain/Superfetch thrashing, or background malware activity. Disabling non-essential startup apps in Task Manager and running anti-malware scans frees up disk bandwidth. Unplugging fans causes thermal shutdown, disabling paging causes out-of-memory crashes, and pulling power corrupts data.

distractor_analysis.1: Unplugging the CPU fan causes immediate thermal throttling and emergency CPU shutdown due to overheating.
distractor_analysis.2: Disabling the paging file completely causes memory exhaustion crashes when RAM-intensive applications allocate memory.
distractor_analysis.3: Disconnecting power during active disk writes causes severe NTFS file system corruption and data loss.

core2.question: A mobile device cannot download or install a required OS security update due to an 'Insufficient Storage Available' error. What is the BEST first action?
options: Replace the handset, since the storage chip has worn out
Point the Wi-Fi DNS at 127.0.0.1 to force a local update cache
Turn on Airplane Mode so the update downloads over cellular later
Offload unused apps, clear caches, and move old photos and video off the device
core2.explanation: Mobile operating system updates require several gigabytes of free scratch space to download and unpack installation packages. Freeing storage by removing unused apps, clearing media caches, and offloading photos to cloud storage provides the required capacity. Chipset replacement is impossible on mobile devices, loopback DNS breaks internet, and Airplane Mode stops updates.

distractor_analysis.1: A full volume is not a worn volume, and the internal flash is not a serviceable part.
distractor_analysis.2: 127.0.0.1 is the device itself, so name resolution stops working entirely.
distractor_analysis.3: Airplane Mode disables the radios, so nothing downloads at all.

core2.question: When opening a web browser, a user is immediately redirected to a deceptive website flashing red banners claiming 'System Heavily Infected - Call Tech Support Now'. What is the root cause?
options: A successful HSTS web certificate negotiation
The Ethernet switch port is configured for full duplex
Adware, browser hijacking, or a malicious browser extension displaying scareware
The motherboard TPM 2.0 chip is functioning properly
core2.explanation: Fake virus warnings in web browsers accompanied by emergency phone numbers are scareware / social engineering scams delivered via adware or compromised browser extensions (browser hijacking). TPM chips, HSTS security headers, and full-duplex switch ports are legitimate, healthy system components.

distractor_analysis.1: TPM 2.0 provides hardware cryptographic storage and does not generate web browser scareware pop-ups.
distractor_analysis.2: HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) enforces HTTPS encryption and prevents unencrypted downgrades.
distractor_analysis.3: Full-duplex switch ports allow simultaneous bidirectional network transmission without generating browser pop-ups.

core2.question: A domain user's profile fails to load in Windows, displaying a temporary profile notification. Where should the technician investigate to identify the root cause and repair the profile?
options: Reset the display adapter driver and set the refresh rate back to 60 Hz
Check the User Profile Service log in Event Viewer, then the ProfileList registry subkey
Rebuild the search index from Indexing Options in Control Panel
Clear the print spooler cache and restart the Print Spooler service
core2.explanation: Temporary profiles occur when Windows cannot load a user's `NTUSER.DAT` hive. Investigating the Application event log (User Profile Service events) and checking `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList` for a SID ending with `.bak` reveals the profile corruption so it can be cleared and rebuilt. Monitor refresh rates, printer spoolers, and fan curves have no relation to user profile hives.

distractor_analysis.1: A broken search index slows Explorer searches. It has no bearing on whether the profile hive loads.
distractor_analysis.2: Spooler faults break printing only. The temporary profile message comes from the User Profile Service.
distractor_analysis.3: Display driver work fixes rendering faults, not profile load failures.

core2.question: A Windows workstation continuously reboots before reaching the logon screen. Which recovery environment should the technician boot into to run Startup Repair or access System Restore?
options: Printer diagnostic utility
macOS Recovery Assistant on another PC
BIOS monitor color calibration tool
Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE)
core2.explanation: The Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) is the dedicated diagnostic and repair platform for Windows, accessible via boot media or after three consecutive failed boots. WinRE provides Startup Repair, System Restore, Command Prompt, and Safe Mode options. Printer tools, macOS recovery, and BIOS color tools cannot repair Windows boot loaders.

distractor_analysis.1: Printer diagnostic utilities test ink nozzles and paper feeds, lacking operating system bootloader repair capabilities.
distractor_analysis.2: macOS Recovery is designed exclusively for Apple Macintosh hardware and operating systems.
distractor_analysis.3: BIOS color calibration adjusts display panel contrast without repairing Windows boot loader binaries.

core2.question: A corporate smartphone battery drains completely within four hours while the phone feels warm in standby mode. Which software diagnostic step should be taken first?
options: Enable mobile hotspot while streaming 4K video
Ignore thermal warnings and charge with an uncertified fast charger
Review Settings -> Battery to identify runaway background apps and inspect background refresh permissions
Increase screen brightness to maximum permanently
core2.explanation: Rapid battery drain accompanied by thermal heat on an idle mobile device points to a rogue background process, runaway app synchronization loop, location tracking abuse, or crypto-mining malware. Checking Settings -> Battery displays detailed power consumption per app, allowing the technician to restrict background activity or uninstall the misbehaving app. Max brightness, hotspots, and uncertified chargers worsen heat and drain.

distractor_analysis.1: Setting screen brightness to 100% places maximum power draw on the display backlight, accelerating battery discharge.
distractor_analysis.2: Running mobile hotspots while streaming video stresses CPU and cellular radios, generating extreme heat.
distractor_analysis.3: Using uncertified fast chargers on an overheating phone risks triggering battery thermal runaway and combustion.

core2.question: A legacy business application fails with 'Access Denied' errors for standard non-administrative users because it attempts to write user configuration logs directly into `C:\Program Files`. What is the BEST long-term remediation?
options: Grant Everyone Modify on the whole Program Files tree
Redirect the application to write under %LocalAppData%, or grant granular folder rights
Add every standard user to the local Administrators group
Turn off User Account Control on all workstations by policy
core2.explanation: Windows security architecture protects `C:\Program Files` from standard user write operations. Applications should write user logs and settings to `%LocalAppData%` or `%AppData%`. If the software cannot be reconfigured, granting granular Write/Modify NTFS permissions strictly to the application's specific subfolder maintains least privilege. Granting admin rights, disabling UAC, or using FAT32 destroys enterprise security.

distractor_analysis.1: Making users administrators fixes one app by removing protection from the entire machine.
distractor_analysis.2: Disabling UAC removes elevation prompts estate-wide and still leaves the file rights wrong.
distractor_analysis.3: Opening the whole Program Files tree lets any process rewrite installed binaries.

core2.question: Why do Mobile Device Management (MDM) systems flag jailbroken (iOS) or rooted (Android) smartphones as non-compliant and block corporate access?
options: Rooting raises radio power beyond the regulatory limit for the region
Jailbreaking disables the SIM slot, so the device cannot be traced
Rooted devices cannot render encrypted attachments in the mail client
Rooting removes kernel sandboxing, so platform controls no longer protect data
core2.explanation: Rooting and jailbreaking bypass operating system privilege boundaries and disable kernel security controls (such as application sandboxing, code signing enforcement, and secure boot checks). This allows malicious apps to access corporate data, capture keystrokes, and intercept communications, creating unacceptable risk that causes MDM policies to revoke access. It does not alter Wi-Fi limits, SIM hardware, or PDF rendering.

distractor_analysis.1: Transmit power is fixed by the radio firmware and regulatory tables, not by root access.
distractor_analysis.2: Jailbreaking is a software change. The SIM slot keeps working.
distractor_analysis.3: Rendering still works. The concern is that nothing stops a malicious app reading that data.

video_reference.title: Troubleshooting Mobile Device Security - CompTIA A+ 220-1202 - 3.3

core2.question: A user's workstation displays persistent pop-up alerts from 'Antivirus Clean Master Pro' demanding payment to clean 50 infected files, even though Windows Defender is healthy. How should the technician remediate this?
options: Turn off Defender so the two scanning engines stop conflicting
Reimage the workstation before collecting any evidence
Treat it as scareware, scan with trusted tools, remove the rogue extension, and brief the user
Pay the fee so the pop-ups stop, then reclaim it on expenses
core2.explanation: Fake antivirus alerts that demand payment are scareware designed to defraud users. Technicians should treat them as malware: isolate the system, remove suspicious programs and browser add-ons, run full scans with legitimate enterprise antimalware, and educate the user (Step 7 of CompTIA methodology). Paying extortion funds crime, disabling Defender leaves machines defenseless, and reformatting SANs causes massive collateral downtime.

distractor_analysis.1: Paying funds the operation and buys nothing. The product is fake.
distractor_analysis.2: Defender is the healthy engine here. Disabling it removes the only real protection on the box.
distractor_analysis.3: Reimaging is disproportionate for scareware and destroys the evidence of how it arrived.

core2.question: A Windows background service configured with an 'Automatic' startup type fails to start upon system boot, causing dependent applications to crash. Where should the technician look to diagnose the specific service failure reason?
options: Open Resource Monitor and watch the handle count for the service
Open services.msc for dependencies, then read the System log in Event Viewer
Open Reliability Monitor and export the stability index history
Open Task Scheduler and check the triggers on the logon tasks
core2.explanation: When an Automatic service fails to start, opening `services.msc` allows technicians to verify the service account credentials, startup parameters, and prerequisites on the Dependencies tab. Concurrently, checking the Windows `System` log in Event Viewer (filtering for Service Control Manager Event IDs 7000, 7001, 7009) provides exact error codes (e.g., logon failure, timeout, missing binary). Display calibration, mouse trails, and emoji settings are irrelevant.

distractor_analysis.1: Reliability Monitor summarises stability trends. It does not give the service error code.
distractor_analysis.2: Task Scheduler runs tasks, not services, so the failing item will not appear there.
distractor_analysis.3: Resource Monitor needs a running process. The service never started.

core2.question: Domain users cannot authenticate to network shares or log into workstations, receiving Kerberos authentication errors. The technician discovers the workstation clock is 12 minutes ahead of the Domain Controller. What is the root cause and remediation?
options: The workstation has lost its computer account password with the domain
The DNS suffix search order no longer lists the internal domain
The site link cost is forcing authentication to a distant domain controller
Kerberos allows only five minutes of clock skew; sync the workstation to the DC time source
core2.explanation: Kerberos authentication uses timestamps inside tickets to prevent replay attacks and enforces a strict maximum clock skew threshold (default: 5 minutes) between clients and Domain Controllers. If the client clock drifts beyond 5 minutes, Kerberos ticket validation fails completely. Resynchronizing system time via NTP (`w32tm /resync`) resolves the issue. Link speed, desoldering TPMs, and FAT32 are destructive or irrelevant.

distractor_analysis.1: A broken machine account gives a trust relationship error, and the clock skew here is the stated fact.
distractor_analysis.2: A suffix problem shows as a name that cannot be found, not as a Kerberos time error.
distractor_analysis.3: A distant DC adds latency. It does not produce a skew error when the clock itself is wrong.

core2.question: A user's corporate smartphone connects to Wi-Fi normally, but cellular mobile data fails completely after traveling overseas. What basic checks should the technician perform FIRST?
options: Check the VPN profile, since a stale tunnel blocks all mobile data
Check that Airplane Mode is off and Bluetooth tethering is disabled
Check Cellular Data, Data Roaming, SIM or eSIM status, and the carrier APN
Check Wi-Fi Assist and the DNS servers set on the Wi-Fi profile
core2.explanation: Cellular data failures after international travel typically stem from: 1. Data Roaming being disabled in Settings, 2. Cellular Data toggle turned off, 3. Inactive or invalid carrier roaming profile, or 4. Misconfigured Access Point Name (APN) settings. RAID cache, GPU VRAM, and POST LEDs are server/desktop hardware components not found on smartphones.

distractor_analysis.1: Wi-Fi already works, so the Wi-Fi profile is not the fault domain. The cellular path is.
distractor_analysis.2: A stale tunnel would break Wi-Fi traffic as well. Wi-Fi is healthy, so the VPN is not the blocker.
distractor_analysis.3: Airplane Mode would kill Wi-Fi too, and tethering does not gate the device's own data path.

core2.question: Following an incomplete application uninstallation, multiple desktop programs fail to launch with errors stating that required DLL files are missing. What is the proper resolution?
options: Copy the DLL from another workstation into the System32 directory
Repair or reinstall the application and its Visual C++ runtime packages
Register the missing DLL manually with regsvr32 from any download site
Roll the machine back to a restore point from before Windows was installed
core2.explanation: Missing DLL errors occur when shared libraries are deleted or unlinked during incomplete software removals. Repairing the application, reinstalling the software, or running the official Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable / .NET installers restores the missing shared DLL binaries in `%SystemRoot%\System32` or application folders. Patch cables, DHCP leases, and exFAT formatting do not replace software DLLs.

distractor_analysis.1: Pulling a system library off a random download site is a malware delivery route, not a fix.
distractor_analysis.2: Restore points only exist after installation. There is no point earlier than the build itself.
distractor_analysis.3: Hand-copying a DLL leaves the registration and version dependencies wrong, so the fault returns.

core2.question: A traveling executive working on an airplane without internet access cannot open a Rights-Managed (IRM) encrypted email attachment on their laptop. What is the technical requirement causing this limitation?
options: The attachment uses a compression codec the offline mail client cannot unpack
Cached Exchange mode strips attachments over 25 MB while the client is offline
The laptop clock has drifted, so the message signing certificate reads as expired
IRM content needs the licensing server to issue a use license, unless credentials were cached offline
core2.explanation: Information Rights Management (IRM) and encrypted messaging protect data by requiring client software to communicate with a centralized rights management server (e.g., Azure Information Protection) to validate permissions and acquire decryption keys. Without internet connectivity, opening encrypted files fails unless rights and licenses were pre-cached for offline access. Heatsinks, Cat 3 cables, and ISA slots are unrelated.

distractor_analysis.1: IRM failures are a licensing problem, not a compression problem. The client can unpack the container; it cannot get a use license.
distractor_analysis.2: Cached mode does not strip attachments by size. The file is present on disk and still will not open.
distractor_analysis.3: Clock drift breaks certificate validation and would show a signature warning, not a rights management prompt.

core2.question: A shared network printer queue becomes unresponsive, with ten print jobs displaying 'Error - Printing' that cannot be canceled. What software troubleshooting procedure clears the stuck queue?
options: Restart the Remote Procedure Call service so the queue re-registers
Flush the local DNS cache so the print server name resolves again
Stop the Print Spooler service, clear the PRINTERS spool folder, then start the service
Delete and re-add the printer using the vendor v4 driver package
core2.explanation: When print jobs lock up in Windows, stopping the Print Spooler service (`net stop spooler`), deleting the corrupt spool files (`.shd` and `.spl`) from `C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS`, and restarting the service (`net start spooler`) purges the stuck print queue and restores printing. Thermal paste, BIOS splash screens, and NX bits have no relationship with printer spoolers.

distractor_analysis.1: Reinstalling the queue may help a driver fault, but the stuck spool files stay on disk and jam the new queue too.
distractor_analysis.2: RPC is a system service other components depend on. Restarting it is disruptive and does not clear spool files.
distractor_analysis.3: Name resolution is fine, since the jobs reached the queue. The spool folder is the blockage.

core2.question: Windows displays a 'Your computer is low on memory' alert when a user opens multiple memory-intensive CAD models and browser tabs. What is the BEST immediate software action?
options: Uninstall the network adapter driver to free kernel pool memory
Close unused applications, check commit charge in Task Manager, and plan a RAM upgrade
Delete the System32 directory to reclaim space on the C: drive
Turn off the paging file so Windows stops swapping to disk
core2.explanation: Low memory warnings occur when combined physical RAM and paging file commit limits are reached. The immediate resolution is closing high-memory applications and background processes via Task Manager. For chronic workloads, installing additional physical RAM modules provides a permanent solution. Deleting System32, disabling paging, and deleting NIC drivers cause system destruction or outages.

distractor_analysis.1: Deleting System32 destroys the installation. The warning is about memory, not disk space.
distractor_analysis.2: Removing the paging file makes low-memory conditions worse and forces hard application failures.
distractor_analysis.3: A network driver holds a trivial amount of pool memory and removing it drops the machine off the network.

core2.question: An employee flashes an unsupported older operating system version onto their corporate smartphone. The MDM console immediately marks the device non-compliant. What is the expected MDM policy response?
options: The employee is automatically granted Domain Administrator privileges
The enterprise Active Directory database is permanently deleted
Corporate network firewalls are disabled automatically
Corporate email, VPN, and resource access are automatically revoked until the device is updated to an approved, patched OS version
core2.explanation: MDM compliance policies mandate minimum operating system versions and security patch levels to ensure known vulnerabilities are closed. When a device runs an unsupported or downgraded OS build, the MDM posture engine flags it as non-compliant and revokes corporate data access (email, Microsoft 365, internal VPN) via conditional access. It does not grant domain admin rights or disable firewalls.

distractor_analysis.1: Non-compliant devices are restricted from corporate access, never granted elevated Domain Admin rights.
distractor_analysis.2: MDM compliance evaluations affect individual endpoints and never delete central Active Directory databases.
distractor_analysis.3: Enterprise network perimeter firewalls are completely unaffected by individual mobile device compliance states.

video_reference.title: Troubleshooting Mobile Device Security - CompTIA A+ 220-1202 - 3.3

core2.question: In which scenario is using Windows System Restore (`rstrui.exe`) the MOST appropriate recovery solution?
options: When the disk reports SMART errors and the volume will not mount
When the machine is being rebuilt for a different user and department
When a recent install or driver update caused instability and a restore point exists
When user documents were deleted and need to be recovered from disk
core2.explanation: Windows System Restore is designed to revert system files, registry keys, installed drivers, and software packages to a previously created snapshot (restore point) without altering user personal documents, making it ideal for rolling back unstable software or bad driver installations. It does not configure router BGP protocols, test fiber optics, or repair cracked screens.

distractor_analysis.1: System Restore does not roll back user documents. Use file history or the backup for that.
distractor_analysis.2: Failing media is a hardware problem. A restore point on that disk cannot be trusted or read.
distractor_analysis.3: A rebuild for a new owner calls for a clean image, not a rollback of the old state.

core2.question: An application displays garbled text, missing glyphs, and overlapping UI characters after a user manually installed unverified third-party font packages. How should the technician resolve this?
options: Flash the motherboard Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) firmware
Restore default Windows system fonts and remove corrupted third-party font packages in Settings -> Personalization -> Fonts
Replace all power supply cables inside the computer chassis
Change the RAID controller stripe size
core2.explanation: Corrupted or incompatible third-party font packages can break application UI rendering and text display. Navigating to Settings -> Personalization -> Fonts and restoring default system fonts or removing corrupt font files resolves the rendering glitches. Power cables, RAID stripe sizes, and BMC firmware have no role in application typography rendering.

distractor_analysis.1: Power supply internal modular cables deliver DC electricity and cannot cause application font rendering glitches.
distractor_analysis.2: Modifying RAID stripe size requires reformatting the storage array and has zero connection to font rendering.
distractor_analysis.3: BMC firmware manages out-of-band server hardware telemetry, completely unrelated to desktop typography.

core2.question: A corporate workstation suddenly fails to connect to the secure 802.1X corporate Wi-Fi network, while other devices connect normally. Event logs show certificate validation failure because the client digital certificate expired yesterday. What is the proper remediation?
options: Disable the wireless network adapter permanently
Configure a static APIPA address (169.254.1.1) on the Wi-Fi adapter
Disable all wireless encryption on corporate access points
Renew and re-enroll the client digital certificate through the enterprise Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) / MDM portal
core2.explanation: 802.1X enterprise wireless with EAP-TLS requires valid, unexpired X.509 client certificates to authenticate endpoints to the RADIUS server. When a client certificate passes its expiration date, authentication is rejected. Renewing or re-enrolling the certificate via the corporate PKI/MDM resolves the failure. Disabling Wi-Fi, using APIPA, or removing encryption on enterprise APs is wrong.

distractor_analysis.1: Disabling the network adapter cuts off wireless capability permanently rather than solving the expired certificate.
distractor_analysis.2: APIPA addresses are non-routable link-local IPs that do not authenticate to 802.1X enterprise networks.
distractor_analysis.3: Disabling encryption across corporate access points exposes all company network traffic to cleartext interception.

core2.question: After entering credentials at the Windows login screen, the desktop appears completely black with only a visible, moving mouse cursor. What is the FASTEST recovery action?
options: Replace the external monitor cable and power strip
Permanently disable the keyboard in Device Manager
Press `Ctrl + Shift + Esc` to open Task Manager, click 'Run new task', and launch `explorer.exe`
Immediately shred the physical SSD in an industrial grinder
core2.explanation: A black screen with a functional mouse cursor after login indicates that the user profile loaded but the Windows graphical shell process (`explorer.exe`) hung or failed to initialize. Pressing `Ctrl + Shift + Esc` launches Task Manager directly, where selecting 'Run new task' and typing `explorer.exe` manually restarts the desktop interface, taskbar, and icons. Shredding SSDs, replacing cables, and disabling keyboards are incorrect.

distractor_analysis.1: Shredding the storage drive destroys the hardware and user data when a simple process restart resolves the issue.
distractor_analysis.2: The monitor cable is working perfectly because the mouse cursor is clearly visible on screen.
distractor_analysis.3: Disabling the keyboard prevents all user input and does not initialize the Windows desktop shell.

core2.question: A technician runs `sfc /scannow` on a crashing Windows machine, but it reports: 'Windows Resource Protection found corrupt files but was unable to fix some of them.' Why is executing `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` the proper next step?
options: It clears the SoftwareDistribution download cache and nothing else
It rebuilds the WinSxS component store from Windows Update sources so the next SFC pass succeeds
It rewrites the boot configuration data store so Windows can find the system partition
It runs a full chkdsk pass that relocates bad clusters before SFC retries
core2.explanation: The System File Checker (`sfc`) relies on the local Windows Component Store (`WinSxS`) to obtain replacement files. If the Component Store itself is corrupted, SFC cannot repair damaged files. Running `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` connects to Windows Update to download healthy replacement component packages, repairing the source repository so a subsequent `sfc /scannow` can successfully complete. DISM does not repair hardware, RAID, or BGP.

distractor_analysis.1: Rewriting the BCD is bootrec work. The machine already boots; the component store is what is damaged.
distractor_analysis.2: chkdsk fixes file system metadata and bad sectors. It does not replace corrupt protected system files.
distractor_analysis.3: Clearing SoftwareDistribution resets the update client. It supplies no replacement component store payload.

core2.question: A datacenter engineer needs to modify inbound firewall rules on production database clusters. Which formalized operational process mandates submitting an RFC, assessing risk, obtaining Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval, and documenting a rollback plan?
options: Shadow IT unapproved implementation
Uncoordinated weekend maintenance
Bypassing tickets to speed up delivery
Formal Change Management process
core2.explanation: Change Management is the formal governance framework designed to minimize outages and business disruption caused by changes. It requires submitting a Request for Change (RFC), performing risk analysis, testing in a sandbox, scheduling within a maintenance window, obtaining CAB approval, and preparing a validated rollback plan. Shadow IT and skipping approvals cause enterprise outages.

distractor_analysis.1: Shadow IT refers to unauthorized, undocumented hardware or software deployments that bypass corporate IT oversight.
distractor_analysis.2: Uncoordinated changes without documented plans or CAB approval lead to unexpected production downtime.
distractor_analysis.3: Bypassing ticketing systems eliminates audit trails and violates compliance and governance policies.

core2.question: Which backup rule specifies maintaining three copies of data, stored across two different media types, with at least one copy kept in an offsite or cloud location?
options: A single USB thumb drive left plugged into the server
Taking desktop screenshots of critical files
The 3-2-1 backup rule
RAID 0 storage striping alone
core2.explanation: The 3-2-1 backup rule is the foundational standard for enterprise data protection: 3 copies of data (production + 2 backups), stored on 2 different media types (e.g., disk array + tape or cloud), with 1 copy stored Offsite. RAID 0 provides zero redundancy, single USB drives lack offsite protection, and screenshots are not database backups.

distractor_analysis.1: RAID 0 stripes data across drives with zero fault tolerance; if one drive fails, all data on the array is lost.
distractor_analysis.2: Leaving a single USB flash drive connected to the server provides zero media diversity and fails if the server room burns down.
distractor_analysis.3: Taking screenshots is not a viable or restorable enterprise database backup strategy.

core2.question: Before opening a server chassis to install additional DDR5 RAM modules, what electrostatic discharge (ESD) safety precautions should a technician take?
options: Spray liquid glass cleaner directly onto the RAM golden edge contacts
Wear an antistatic ESD wrist strap connected to unpainted chassis metal and work on a grounded ESD mat
Wear a heavy wool sweater and shuffle feet on carpet
Place open electronic circuit boards directly on conductive aluminum foil while powered
core2.explanation: Electrostatic discharge (ESD) can destroy delicate semiconductor circuitry with voltages far below human perception. Technicians must wear a properly grounded ESD wrist strap, work on an ESD-safe dissipative mat, handle memory modules by their non-conductive edges, and store components in antistatic bags. Wool clothes generate static, foil shorts live circuits, and liquids corrode contacts.

distractor_analysis.1: Wool clothing and walking across carpet generate thousands of volts of static electricity, drastically increasing ESD risk.
distractor_analysis.2: Placing powered circuit boards on conductive foil creates immediate short circuits and destroys electronics.
distractor_analysis.3: Spraying liquid cleaners onto gold contacts causes corrosion, liquid ingress, and electrical shorts.

core2.question: Which safety document must be consulted to review handling, storage, and emergency spill response protocols for hazardous datacenter substances such as printer toner, isopropyl alcohol, or UPS battery acid?
options: GPU overclocking profile
DNS zone transfer record
VLAN trunking protocol configuration
Safety Data Sheet (SDS / MSDS)
core2.explanation: Safety Data Sheets (SDS), formerly known as MSDS, are federally mandated documents detailing the chemical composition, health hazards, personal protective equipment (PPE), safe handling procedures, and emergency spill/first-aid instructions for hazardous substances. GPU profiles, DNS records, and VLAN configs have no safety information.

distractor_analysis.1: GPU overclocking profiles configure graphics clock speeds and voltages, providing zero chemical safety guidance.
distractor_analysis.2: DNS zone transfer records manage domain name replication between nameservers.
distractor_analysis.3: VLAN trunking protocols manage layer 2 virtual network tags across network switches.

core2.question: During an incident response investigation where a corporate laptop is seized for legal evidence, why is maintaining a strict 'Chain of Custody' form critical?
options: It authorizes the technician to open and read the user's personal files
It sets the retention period before the laptop can be reimaged
It documents everyone who handled the media, which keeps the evidence admissible
It records the exact imaging tool version used during acquisition
core2.explanation: Chain of Custody is the formal chronological documentation recording the seizure, custody, transfer, analysis, and disposition of physical and electronic evidence. Maintaining an unbroken chain of custody ensures that evidence has not been tampered with and remains legally admissible in a court of law. Wallpapers, fan curves, and cable colors are unrelated.

distractor_analysis.1: Tool and hash detail belong on the acquisition record. Chain of custody tracks possession over time.
distractor_analysis.2: Custody paperwork does not grant a technician permission to browse content. Legal counsel scopes that.
distractor_analysis.3: Retention and disposal come from the evidence handling policy, after the case closes.

core2.question: How does a ticketing system primarily assist IT operations teams in daily service delivery?
options: By assigning public IPv4 blocks to each branch office
By logging, prioritizing, assigning and tracking requests so SLA targets are met
By replacing the hardware monitoring platform used in the NOC
By removing the need for a separate knowledge base
core2.explanation: Ticketing systems (such as ServiceNow or Jira Service Desk) provide a centralized platform to record, categorize, prioritize, assign, track, and document customer incidents and requests, ensuring accountability, historical knowledge capture, and compliance with contractual SLAs. They do not replace hardware monitoring, eliminate documentation, or allocate IPv4 space.

distractor_analysis.1: Monitoring detects faults. Ticketing tracks the work that follows and does not replace it.
distractor_analysis.2: A knowledge base holds the how. The ticket queue holds the what and the when.
distractor_analysis.3: Address allocation is an IPAM function and has no relationship to service delivery tracking.

core2.question: What is the primary operational purpose of affixing barcode asset tags to company hardware and maintaining Configuration Management Database (CMDB) records?
options: To give the service desk a warranty lookup for each monitor model
To let finance depreciate assets on a fixed annual schedule
To keep firmware revisions aligned across a switch stack
To track configuration items across their whole lifecycle, from procurement to disposal
core2.explanation: Asset management and CMDB tracking record detailed information about physical and logical Configuration Items (CIs)-including serial numbers, location, assigned user, warranty dates, purchase costs, and relationships-throughout their entire lifecycle from procurement to disposal. Asset tags have no effect on monitor pixels, beep code volume, or printer fusers.

distractor_analysis.1: Warranty lookup is one report the CMDB can feed. It is not why the database exists.
distractor_analysis.2: Depreciation is a finance use of the same data, downstream of the asset record itself.
distractor_analysis.3: Firmware alignment is handled by configuration management tooling on the devices.

core2.question: When communicating with an upset, frustrated customer whose workstation crashed during a payroll run, how should the technician conduct the interaction?
options: Transfer the call to another queue so the user can cool down first
